Application Materials.content:
After submitting the application, applicants for the Master of Social Sciences in the field of Social Data Analytics should upload supporting documents via the system for the University’s preliminary consideration. **All documents should be submitted within one month starting from the date applicants receive the email notification or by the deadline as stipulated in the email.** Application number should be included on the file name of each document.
Abbreviations for file naming:
- T: Transcript
- P: Personal Statement
- G: Graduation Certificate
- C: CV
- B: Bachelor Certificate
- N: Name Changing Proof
- E: Proof of English Proficiency
- O: Other Certificates
- ID: Identity Documents
Transcripts, diplomas, certificates, and other submitted documents that are not in English should be accompanied by a certified English translation produced by the issuing authority concerned. Applicants are **NOT REQUIRED** to submit original/certified true copies of documents to the University during the application stage.
Application Checklist of Supporting Documents:
- Identity Documents: local applicants: Hong Kong ID Card; non-local applicants from Mainland China: Mainland ID Card/Passport; non-local applicants from other countries/regions: Passport.
- Official Transcripts: final transcript for a completed degree that includes the degree conferment information, or latest available transcript for a degree that is currently in progress or has not yet been conferred.
- Institution Grading System: transcript legends, keys or grading scales which are normally available on the back of the transcript or in the student handbook.
- Degree Certificates: for applicants whose degrees have been awarded/conferred at the time of application, a copy of the Degree Certificates should be provided.
- For applicants whose qualifications were awarded by universities or comparable institutions in Mainland China: Online Verification Report of Higher Education Qualification Certificate and Online Verification Report of Higher Education Degree Certificate, in both Chinese and English versions. The validity period should be set to six months or the longest available duration.
- For non-local applicants from Mainland China whose qualifications were awarded by overseas universities/institutions: Overseas Credentials Evaluation Report issued by CSCSE, or if not yet available, an email or text message sent by CSCSE after payment confirming that the application of the Report has been successfully initiated.
- English Language Requirements documents, where applicable: TOEFL / IELTS / GCE / IGCSE / Cambridge Test of Proficiency in English Language results, or an official letter or equivalent proof such as transcript or degree certificate confirming that the qualification was obtained where the medium of instruction is English.
- Two referee reports sent via the online application system. Only referees with official university/company email/correspondence addresses are accepted.
- Personal Statement: reasons for interest in this programme, the benefits expected from this programme, and future career/study plan.
- CV.

Academic Requirements.content:
- Applicants must comply with the [**General Regulations**](https://calendar.hku.hk/general-regulations/).
- Applicants must **hold a Bachelor’s Degree or an Equivalent Qualification**.
- Applicants shall preferably have a Bachelor’s degree in one of the fields of social sciences: Anthropology, Cognitive Science, Communication, Economics, Education Studies, Ethnic Studies, Linguistics, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, Urban Studies and Planning, or a closely related field.
- Applicants shall preferably have pre-existing training in statistics and/or formal logic or prior experience with one or more technical domains, including programming, statistics, formal logic, calculus, linear algebra, etc.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Applicants seeking admission on the basis of a qualification from a university or comparable institution outside Hong Kong of which the language of teaching and/or examination is not English must satisfy the University English language requirement applicable to higher degrees.
Required examination result: one of the following:
- TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language): **a score of 80 or above**; or
- IELTS (International English Language Testing System): **a minimum overall band of 6 with no subtest lower than 5.5**; or
- GCE (Overseas General Certificate of Education): **Grade C or above**; or
- IGCSE (International General Certificate of Secondary Education): **Grade C or above**; or
- Cambridge Test of Proficiency in English Language: **Grade C or above**.
An application for exemption from the above requirements shall be considered on a case by case basis. Unless in exceptional circumstances, the applicant is exempted from this requirement by the relevant Board of the Faculty or Board of Studies, in the case of higher degrees by coursework.
Starting from the 2026 intake, **IELTS and TOEFL tests must be taken within two years prior to September 1 of each admissions year**.

Program Overview.content:
Social Data Analytics (SDA) combines the analysis of large or complex data that arise from human and social interactions with social sciences theories and concepts. In the private, public and academic sectors, there is a strong demand for social scientists who are also trained in data science and computationally intensive methods.
MSocSc(SDA) pools computational and quantitative research expertise across the Faculty of Social Sciences to offer students the data analytical skills and prepare them for further doctoral training and to work as data sciences professionals in NGO and governmental agency, business, advertising, marketing, and other jobs across the knowledge economy that require integrating social sciences domain expertise with large datasets in computational systems.
The unique emphasis in Social Data Analytics is on the computational use of formal social sciences theories. This has two specific ends: a) simulating the behaviour of formal theories in computational contexts to generate largescale predictions, often requiring agent-based simulations to predict the behaviours and interactions among complex social systems and networks; and b) interpreting large-scale naturalistic data through the lens of these formal theories to improve generalisation, prediction, and explainability.
Programme Aims:
1. Provide students with the theory, skills and techniques they need to undertake data analytics in a social sciences context, enabling critical thinking and preparing them to work as data science professionals and for further doctoral training.
2. Engender in students an awareness of both the possibilities and limitations of a range of methodological approaches and techniques used across the social sciences in identifying and researching real-world problems.
3. Use teaching informed by research to provide a stimulating culture of learning, the development of high-level research skills, and enthusiasm for applying these within.
The HKU MSocSc(SDA) Programme is a 1-year full-time Programme that consists of a mandatory boot camp and three different categories of courses: (i) compulsory courses, (ii) elective courses, and (iii) capstone project.

Curriculum.content:
Students are required to complete **5** compulsory courses, **3** elective courses and **1** capstone project throughout their studies. Before the commencement of the programme, all students must attend **a mandatory 18-hour social data analytics summer boot camp**. The boot camp will be taught over three to four days, organised around topics including R and RStudio, algebra, probability and statistics, objects and classes in R-Studio, data cleaning/reshaping/restructuring with the tidyverse, basic programming, and communicating/collaborating with RMarkdown, Rpres, Shiny and Github.
**Compulsory Courses**
- **MSDA7001 Introduction to social data analytics** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
- **MSDA7002 Statistical foundations** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
- **MSDA7003 Machine learning** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
- **MSDA7004 Research design and inference in the social sciences** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
- **MSDA7005 Programming for social scientists** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
**Elective Courses**
At least two elective courses from the following list*:
- **MSDA7101 Big data solutions to social problems** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
- **MSDA7102 Simulating human behaviours with agent-based models** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
- **MSDA7103 Text as data: Natural language processing and social research** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
- **MSDA7104 Social network analysis** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
- **MSDA7105 Media data analysis** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
One additional elective course can also be taken from other programmes*:
- **GEOG7308 Machine learning for geospatial data (6 credits)**
- **GEOG7310 Cloud computing for geospatial data analytics (6 credits)**
- **GEOG7311 Web GIS (6 credits)**
- **MPOP7101 Fertility and family structures (6 credits)**
- **MPOP7102 Mortality and health (6 credits)**
- **MPOP7103 Migration and urbanisation (6 credits)**
- **MPOP7105 Demography of Greater China (6 credits)**
- **MSBH7005 Scientific inquiry and research methods in behavioral health (6 credits)**
- **SOCI7006 Research methods in media, culture and creative cities (6 credits)**
- **SOWK6185 Qualitative research methods (6 credits)**
**Capstone project (Compulsory)**
- **MSDA8001 Capstone project** - 12 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework. Students will conduct a research project in close collaboration with supervisors from the programme, applying skills and techniques learned during the taught component to a substantive original research or industry focused problem. Projects will be supervised by academic staff affiliated with the Social Data Analytics programme and may involve desk based research, secondary data sources, primary data collection, or collaboration with an external organisation.
Please [click here](https://www.socsc.hku.hk/sda/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/MSocScSDA_Regulations-and-Syllabuses_2024-2025.pdf) for the regulations, syllabus and course descriptions. *Offering schedule and quota is subject to availability.

Cost of Attendance.content:
The fees and charges below are based on 2024/25 only; actual costs will increase for 2025/26.
- Books and supplies for postgraduate students: around HK$11,100 - HK$53,700 p.a. Some courses also involve significant expenses relating to overseas field trips and special equipment.
- University residential halls & colleges / CEDARS-administered non-hall housing for postgraduate students: HK$19,977 p.a. - HK$115,713 p.a.; HK$23,111 - HK$47,355 p.a. (from the end of August to the end of May); HK$25,931 - HK$89,000 p.a.
- Hall miscellaneous charges: HK$2,000 - HK$3,000 p.a. These include students’ association membership fees, compulsory high table fees, room and/or smartcard deposits, etc., excluding air-conditioning charge which varies with individual lifestyle and seasons (approximately HK$200 per month in summer).
- Compulsory hall meal charges: HK$9,000 - HK$10,000 p.a. (not all meals are covered).
- Privately rented accommodation: single room from HK$50 per sq. ft. up, excluding utilities.
- Food, groceries, transportation and others: around HK$6,100 per month up (depending on your lifestyles and if you go grocery shopping around the campus).
- Other personal expenses: students need to budget for entertainment, overseas travel, insurance and medical expenses, etc.
- Meal expenses: on-campus catering outlets typically cost HK$25 – HK$65 per meal; eateries around the Main Campus are around 10% - 20% higher than campus outlets.
- Transportation cost examples per ride: Sassoon Road to Main Campus HK$2 - HK$7 by University shuttle bus or HK$5.1 – HK$14.5 by bus/minibus; Main Campus to Central HK$5.9 – HK$9.4; Main Campus to Causeway Bay HK$5.9 – HK$12.4; Main Campus to Mongkok HK$13.2 - HK$19.
- For non-local students, expenses for the first month can amount to HK$10,000 or more for a student on top of tuition fees, due to significant extra expenses such as rental charges, household items and textbooks.

Multiple Applications.content: Yes, it is possible for you to apply to multiple programmes at HKU. You can apply under different usernames on the application system and pay the application fee (**HK$600**) for each programme that you wish to apply to. You can only enrol in one programme, even if you receive offers from other programmes.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Can I defer my admission to the next year if I am admitted? A: You shall require to re-apply for admission for the next year.

Conditional Admission Policy.content: Should applicants be given a **conditional offer** by the University, applicants will be notified to submit the stipulated documents. Applicants should take into account the processing time required for the issuance of original/certified true copies of documents and start preparing them at their earliest convenience upon receipt of offer.
